items.stem: Explain the term “autonomic neural system”.
items.answer: The division of the PNS that transmits impulses from the CNS to involuntary organs and smooth muscles.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the division of the PNS that transmits impulses from the CNS to involuntary organs and smooth muscles.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the neural system and the neuron is correct?
items.answer: Myelinated nerve fibres are found in spinal and cranial nerves.
items.markingKey: (c) Myelinated nerve fibres are found in spinal and cranial nerves. The other statements are false. Dendrites carry impulses towards the cell body; the axon carries them away. Unmyelinated fibres are enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath. The CNS comprises the brain and spinal cord; the PNS has all the nerves associated with them.
options: The PNS comprises the brain and spinal cord.
Unmyelinated fibres are enclosed by Schwann cells that form a myelin sheath.
Myelinated nerve fibres are found in spinal and cranial nerves.
Dendrites carry impulses away from the cell body.

items.stem:

items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: The CNS comprises the brain and spinal cord; the PNS has all the nerves associated with them.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A neuron has these features: no dendrites; cell body with one axon only. Identify the type of neuron. Give a reason.
items.answer: A unipolar neuron
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a unipolar neuron; 1 mark: the features no dendrites; cell body with one axon only are characteristic of it.

items.stem:

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Saltatory conduction from node to node is faster.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
In a prepared slide, Ishita saw a neuron with a cell body containing granules, many short branched processes and one long process covered by a sheath with regular gaps.
(i) Name the granules in the cell body. (1 mark)
(ii) Name the short processes and the long process. (1 mark)
(iii) What are the sheath and the gaps called, and which cells form the sheath? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Nissl's granules. (ii) Dendrites; axon. (iii) Myelin sheath and nodes of Ranvier; Schwann cells.

items.stem: Which term describes a long fibre that transmits nerve impulses away from the cell body to a synapse or neuromuscular junction?
items.answer: axon

options: autonomic neural system
myelin sheath
Nissl's granules
axon

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a unipolar neuron and a multipolar neuron on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A neuron has these features: two or more dendrites. Identify the type of neuron – a unipolar neuron or a multipolar neuron? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) A unipolar neuron: cell body with one axon only; no dendrites; usually found in the embryonic stage. A multipolar neuron: one axon; two or more dendrites; found in the cerebral cortex. (b) A multipolar neuron.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: a multipolar neuron; 1 mark: “two or more dendrites” is a feature of a multipolar neuron.

items.stem: Describe the divisions of the human neural system.
items.answer: CNS – brain and spinal cord, site of information processing and control; PNS – all nerves (cranial and spinal) associated with the CNS; afferent fibres carry impulses to the CNS and efferent fibres from it; PNS divided into somatic (to skeletal muscles) and autonomic (to involuntary organs and smooth muscles), which is further divided into sympathetic and parasympathetic.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.answer: (a) A multipolar neuron: one axon; two or more dendrites; found in the cerebral cortex. A unipolar neuron: cell body with one axon only; no dendrites; usually found in the embryonic stage. (b) A multipolar neuron.

items.stem: Explain the term “Nissl's granules”.
items.answer: Granular bodies found in the cytoplasm of the cell body and dendrites of a neuron.

items.stem: Define the term “depolarisation”.
items.answer: The reversal of polarity at a site of stimulation, making the outer surface negative and the inner surface positive.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the reversal of polarity at a site of stimulation, making the outer surface negative and the inner surface positive.

items.answer: The fluid outside the axon has a low concentration of K⁺ and a high concentration of Na⁺.

items.stem: Distinguish between electrical and chemical synapses on three points.
items.answer: Electrical – pre- and post-synaptic membranes in very close proximity; current flows directly; very fast; rare. Chemical – membranes separated by a synaptic cleft; transmission by neurotransmitters; slower; common.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.answer: (i) Repolarising membrane (ii) K⁺ permeability rises (iii) more permeable to K⁺; nearly impermeable to Na⁺

items.stem: Explain the generation and conduction of a nerve impulse. Describe transmission across a chemical synapse.
items.answer: Resting: K⁺ and negative proteins inside, Na⁺ outside; membrane more permeable to K⁺; Na⁺/K⁺ pump 3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in; outside positive – resting potential. Stimulus: Na⁺ permeability rises, Na⁺ influx, polarity reverses – action potential; local currents to the next site; repolarisation by K⁺ efflux. Chemical synapse: impulse at axon terminal, vesicles fuse with membrane, neurotransmitters into cleft, bind receptors on post-synaptic membrane, ion channels open, excitatory or inhibitory potential.
items.markingKey: 3 marks impulse; 2 marks synapse.
